es: Explicar qué tono transmite un mensaje breve, leído o escuchado, y qué expresiones lo producen.

teaching.en: «Finally! Thanks for getting back to me» can read as sarcastic, because the first word suggests that the reply was far too late.
teaching.es: «¡Por fin! Gracias por responderme» puede leerse como sarcástico, porque la primera palabra sugiere que la respuesta llegó demasiado tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Sarcastic: dice una cosa pero critica otra. Read as = interpretarse como.
segments: «Finally! Thanks for getting back to me» can read as sarcastic, because
the first word suggests that the reply was far too late.
teaching.audioText: «Finally! Thanks for getting back to me» can read as sarcastic, because the first word suggests that the reply was far too late.

teaching.en: A curt message such as «Send it now» sounds demanding, whereas «Could you send it when you have a moment?» keeps a friendly tone.
teaching.es: Un mensaje cortante como «Envíalo ya» suena exigente, mientras que «¿Podrías enviarlo cuando tengas un momento?» mantiene un tono amistoso.
teaching.explanationEs: Curt = seco; demanding = orden sin please; could you… + when you have a moment suaviza.
segments: A curt message such as «Send it now» sounds demanding, whereas «Could
you send it when you have a moment?» keeps a friendly tone.
teaching.audioText: A curt message such as «Send it now» sounds demanding, whereas «Could you send it when you have a moment?» keeps a friendly tone.

teaching.en: «I was wondering if you might possibly have time to look at this» is tentative: the writer asks carefully and leaves room to refuse.
teaching.es: «Me preguntaba si por casualidad tendrías tiempo de mirar esto» es prudente: quien escribe pide con cuidado y deja margen para decir que no.
teaching.explanationEs: Tentative: pide con cautela, sin imponer; might + possibly aumentan la distancia.
segments: «I was wondering if you might possibly have time to look at
this» is tentative: the writer asks carefully and leaves room to refuse.
teaching.audioText: «I was wondering if you might possibly have time to look at this» is tentative: the writer asks carefully and leaves room to refuse.

teaching.en: «As I have already explained» sounds cold and slightly condescending, because it treats the reader as someone who has not been paying attention.
teaching.es: «Como ya he explicado» suena frío y algo condescendiente, porque trata al lector como alguien que no ha prestado atención.
teaching.explanationEs: Cold: distancia y reproche; condescending: hablar «desde arriba» al lector.
segments: «As I have already explained» sounds cold and slightly condescending, because it
treats the reader as someone who has not been paying attention.
teaching.audioText: «As I have already explained» sounds cold and slightly condescending, because it treats the reader as someone who has not been paying attention.

teaching.en: A blunt message has no greeting, no please and no thanks, but adding «I'm so sorry to bother you» makes the tone apologetic and softer.
teaching.es: Un mensaje brusco no lleva saludo, ni please ni thanks, pero añadir «Siento mucho molestarte» hace que el tono sea de disculpa y más suave.
teaching.explanationEs: Blunt = directo hasta resultar brusco; apologetic = expresa arrepentimiento o deferencia.
segments: A blunt message has no greeting, no please and no thanks, but adding
«I'm so sorry to bother you» makes the tone apologetic and softer.
teaching.audioText: A blunt message has no greeting, no please and no thanks, but adding «I'm so sorry to bother you» makes the tone apologetic and softer.

teaching.en: If a message could be read as angry, tone down the wording by replacing orders with questions and adding a friendly closing line.
teaching.es: Si un mensaje podría leerse como molesto, suaviza el tono cambiando las órdenes por preguntas y añadiendo una despedida amistosa.
teaching.explanationEs: Tone down = rebajar el tono; las preguntas con could y un cierre amable son las herramientas básicas.
segments: If a message could be read as angry, tone down the wording
by replacing orders with questions and adding a friendly closing line.
teaching.audioText: If a message could be read as angry, tone down the wording by replacing orders with questions and adding a friendly closing line.

prompt.es: Elige el tono del mensaje y la expresión que lo revela.

choices.text: It sounds friendly, because it opens with «Hi Jo» and ends with thanks.
It sounds sarcastic because of «Finally!» and «I suppose that is quick for you».
It sounds tentative, because «I suppose» shows the writer is unsure of the facts.

feedback.es: Finally y el comentario final critican la tardanza con ironía: el agradecimiento es solo la fachada.

hint.es: Busca las palabras que critican la demora sin decirlo abiertamente.

origin.text: Hi Jo. Finally! It only took you three days to answer, but thanks anyway. I suppose that is quick for you.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tu mensaje suena seco: sin saludo, sin please, solo una orden.»

feedback.es: Un mensaje sin saludo ni cortesía, solo con una orden, suena cortante, seco o brusco.

hint.es: Adjetivo que describe un mensaje directo hasta la sequedad.

origin.text: Your message sounds very ___: there is no greeting, no please and no thanks, only an order.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El mensaje puede interpretarse como sarcástico por la palabra Finally.»

answer.text: The message can read as sarcastic because of Finally

feedback.es: Read as + adjetivo describe la interpretación del mensaje; because of señala la expresión responsable.

hint.es: Empieza por The message can y termina con la palabra que causa el tono.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué el equipo reaccionó mal al mensaje de la jefa.

choices.text: Its deadline was so close that the team felt angry and worried.
Its tone was so casual that the team did not take the deadline seriously.
Its wording made the team feel they had not been paying attention.

feedback.es: La jefa quería ser clara, pero «as I already said» trata a los lectores como si no hubieran atendido.

origin.audio: Last Monday my manager sent the team a message that said: As I already said, the report is due at noon. Please do not be late again. Nobody replied for an hour, and then Sara wrote back: Thanks for the reminder, I will send it in ten minutes. Everyone agreed that the message sounded cold and slightly condescending, even though my manager insists she only wanted to be clear. She had not noticed that the words as I already said make readers feel they were not paying attention.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con el tono que crea en el lector.

feedback.es: Cada expresión aporta una actitud: reproche por repetir, prudencia, ironía u orden sin cortesía.

prompt.es: Suaviza el tono de este mensaje cortante.

answer.text: Could you send me the photos when you have a moment? I would really appreciate it.
accepted: Could you send me the photos when you have a moment? I would really appreciate it.
Would you mind sending me the photos when you have a moment? Thank you so much.
Could you please send me the photos when you can? I would be very grateful.

feedback.es: Para suavizar, cambia la orden por una pregunta con could y añade una fórmula de agradecimiento.

origin.text: Send me the photos now. I already asked twice!

evidenceGroups: i was wondering if you could

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz: ¿qué da a entender la hablante sobre su petición?

choices.text: She needs an answer soon, but her tone stays tentative and apologetic.
She is in no hurry, so the listener can reply whenever it suits them.
She is annoyed with the listener, although her words are polite.

feedback.es: «No rush at all» contradice el plazo del viernes: la petición es real, aunque el tono sea prudente y de disculpa.

origin.audio: Hi, it's Mia from the landlord's office. I'm so sorry to bother you again, and I completely understand if this is a bad time, but I was wondering whether you might be able to look at the contract this week, because the deadline is on Friday. No rush at all, of course.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura adopta el autor ante quienes aún no han respondido?

choices.text: He pressures them by naming the people who have not replied yet.
He reminds them kindly and does not blame anyone.
He treats the form as unimportant and entirely optional.

feedback.es: El autor agradece a quien ya respondió y minimiza el esfuerzo para los demás: empuja con suavidad, sin reproche.

origin.text: Hi team, just a quick reminder that the form closes on Friday. Some of you have kindly filled it in already, thank you, and for everyone else it only takes about five minutes. Cheers, Tom

prompt.es: Completa: «La respuesta de Mia sonó sarcástica; todos entendieron lo contrario.»

feedback.es: Decir una cosa y querer decir lo contrario, con intención de crítica, es sarcasmo.

origin.text: Mia's reply sounded ___: she wrote «Oh, brilliant, another meeting!», but everybody knew she meant the opposite.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué propósito termina así su mensaje la hablante.

choices.text: To hint that the driver should now do something for her.
To ask the driver for another lift next week.
To offer something in return and keep the friendship warm.

feedback.es: La última frase ofrece devolver el favor: su fin es mantener la relación cálida, no quejarse ni insinuar deuda.

origin.audio: Thanks so much for the lift yesterday, you were brilliant! I honestly don't know how I would have got there on time otherwise. Let me know if I can return the favour.

prompt.es: ¿Qué tono revela la última frase de la nota de la cocina?

choices.text: It sounds sarcastic, because the thanks is really a reproach.
It sounds apologetic, because the writer admits having said the same thing before.
It sounds friendly, because the writer thanks everybody so warmly.

feedback.es: El agradecimiento exagerado tras un reproche funciona como ironía: critica a quien deja tazas sucias.

origin.text: To everyone who uses the kitchen: as I said last week, dirty cups do not wash themselves. Thank you so much for your help!

prompt.es: Completa: «Sin saludo amable, una respuesta útil puede interpretarse como fría.»

feedback.es: Read as o come across as describen cómo interpreta el lector el tono, sea o no la intención del autor.

origin.text: Without a friendly greeting, even a helpful reply can ___ as cold, however good the writer's intentions may be.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cambia la orden por una pregunta para suavizar el mensaje.»

answer.text: Replace the order with a question to tone down the message

feedback.es: Tone down the message = suavizar el tono; la herramienta es sustituir la orden por una pregunta.
